rows.notes: 'a typical query uses in the range of 0.0 to 0.067 mL of water'; the upper end is given here. Energy: modelled median 0.31 Wh (interquartile range 0.16 to 0.60 Wh) from the Joule paper; long reasoning responses use more than 10x as much. Added in v2026.10.22.

rows.source_title: Daily Memphian (Hardiman), Analyzing xAI's MLGW bills (29 Dec 2025, updated 12 Jan 2026)
rows.notes: 'Colossus had a peak water usage of about 381,000 gallons a day from Aug. 3 to Sept. 4, 2025', from copies of xAI's MLGW bills; projections had been more than 1 million gallons a day.

rows.source_title: Memphis Flyer, Protect Our Aquifer: xAI Bought 25M Gallons of Water from MLGW, Projects Increases (22 May 2026)
rows.publisher: xAI (Protect Our Aquifer, via Memphis Flyer)
rows.unit: million US gallons per month (more than)
rows.notes: 'purchased more than 25 million gallons of water from Memphis Light, Gas, and Water (MLGW) in March'; POA also gives 812,502 gallons a day pumped from the Memphis Sand Aquifer (basis not stated).

rows.source_title: Governing (Smith), Wastewater Will Cool This Memphis Data Center (16 Mar 2026)
rows.unit: million US gallons per day (stated need)
rows.notes: xAI engineer Mark Carroll: the closed loop water 'doesn't need replacing' but 'the open loop at Colossus needs 3 million gallons a day'. Cooling towers evaporate about 85%. Water recycling plant (treated wastewater) under construction since Oct 2025; end-2026 target 'hazy'.

rows.source_title: The Advocate (Abugov), Meta Louisiana data center water (21 Dec 2025)
rows.notes: About 1.5 million gallons a day on average, from the Mississippi River Alluvial Aquifer; closed-loop cooling, no water needed for more than half the year, new water above about 90 F. Meta agreed to voluntary annual water reports for its first five years.

rows.source_title: The Advocate (Abugov), Meta Louisiana data center water (21 Dec 2025)
rows.unit: million US gallons per day (registered, more than)
rows.notes: 'registered to consume more than 23 million gallons of water per day', or 8.4 billion gallons a year, per state records and the company.

rows.source_title: KJZZ (Reznick), Project Blue would have used millions of gallons of Tucson water. Residents, city leaders said no. (11 Aug 2025)
rows.notes: 'at least 1,910 acre feet per year at full build out', about 6% of Tucson's total water supply; potable water for at least the first two years before reclaimed water. City council voted unanimously to end negotiations (Aug 2025). 1,910 acre-feet = about 622 million US gallons at 325,851 gallons per acre-foot (GreenCalculus conversion). 2023 public records tied the project to AWS, which said it had no current commitments.

rows.source_title: KJZZ / AZPM (Mendoza), Project Blue data center could use up to 31 million gallons of water per year (29 May 2026)
rows.unit: million US gallons per year (up to)
rows.notes: Arizona Department of Water Resources: the data center under construction in Pima County 'could use up to 31 million gallons of water per year'; two commercial wells applied for in January 2026.

rows.source_title: Oracle Fact Sheet: Stargate Data Centers (23 Sep 2025)
rows.unit: US gallons per building per year (estimated)
rows.notes: 'The anticipated water usage for cooling system maintenance and quality purposes totals approximately 12,625 gallons per building per year.' Closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling; eight buildings = about 101,000 gallons a year (GreenCalculus calculation).

rows.source_title: Texas Tribune (Martinez, Lozano Carver), Texas data center water use (25 Sep 2025)
rows.notes: 'will initially use 8 million gallons of Abilene city water to fill the cooling system'; the city's average daily use is 22 million gallons. Other outlets report about 1 million gallons.

rows.source_title: Microsoft Local, Understanding water use at Microsoft datacenters
rows.notes: 'uses about as much water as a typical restaurant each year'; no gallon figure published. Over 90% of capacity on closed-loop liquid cooling filled once during construction; the other 10% uses outdoor air, 'switching to water only during the hottest days' (Microsoft blog, 18 Sep 2025: https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/09/18/inside-the-worlds-most-powerful-ai-datacenter/).
'In 2014, data centers consumed 21.2 billion liters of water, with 64% in internal data centers.'

rows.notes: 'The total indirect water footprint of U.S. data centers is nearly 800 billion liters'; 176 TWh in 2023.

rows.notes: 'national average of 4.52 L/kWh of indirect water consumption' for data center electricity, against 4.35 L/kWh for all US electricity.
